title: An anisotropic Biot tensor from mineral stress and distention work
summary: A guide to the constitutive checks, finite-element examples, implementation, and numerical data accompanying the paper. Browse the recorded evidence, download the manuscript and numerical supplement, and follow the commands to reproduce the calculations.

provenance.note: The base commit predates this working revision. The finite-element sources and evidence are provided under the repository-relative paths moose_app/, validation/, fe-evidence/, figures/ and site/; the scientific-snapshot artifact lists the exact files with SHA-256 hashes, and the review snapshot pinned in the review record is the authoritative frozen artifact for the checks below.

analytical.summary: The independent Mandel reference passes 38 self-checks (peak overshoot 5.4659% at t = 0.01516535). This status covers the analytical reference self-checks only.
analytical.demonstration: The finite-load FE comparison against the reference is a demonstration, not an analytical gate; its normalized pressure discrepancy floors at about 3.2e-3 (a discretization floor at nx=20, dt=1e-3) rather than decaying to the linear reference as the load tends to 1e-4.

implementation.summary: Material-point and residual checks: fluid EOS and reference-mass derivatives (110 checks, max scaled error 8.09e-09); conformal constitutive suite; independent spherical-gauge and reconstruction suites. The C++ law matches the independent Python evaluation to 6.4e-14 over 41 finite states (artifact cpp-python-constitutive.json, which records the comparison itself).

convergence.summary: Manufactured-solution L2 convergence at a fixed final time: spatial order is consistent with Q2 displacement and Q1 pressure (ux 2.99/2.96, uy 3.00/2.96, p 2.00/2.00 over nx=4,8,16 at dt=1e-4). The temporal order is measured by successive differences of the exact-solution error norms at fixed mesh, which cancels the mesh-dependent spatial floor; the nx=16 triple (ux 1.093, uy 0.978, p 1.015) bounds the temporal order near one (at most about 1.1), consistent with backward Euler and not higher. At finer meshes the same measure gives nx=32 (ux 1.397, uy 1.018, p 1.125) and nx=64 (ux 1.396, uy 1.076, p 1.252). Those measured successive-difference orders belong to this mesh and step sequence and include values above one (ux is about 1.4); they are reported as measurements and no order above one is asserted. The departure from one at fixed mesh is a mesh-step cross term in the error balance: successive differences cancel a time-step-independent mesh floor exactly, so no order above one is claimed; naive error-ratio orders at fixed step are dominated by the spatial error and are never reported as temporal order. The isotropic Mandel spatial refinement is non-monotone at the finest level because of the initial drainage boundary discontinuity and is reported separately.

finite_deformation.summary: A material-point benchmark verifies full spatial stress and pressure derivatives, independent equilibrium minimization, and the reference limit for an isotropic mineral with commuting finite distention and stress. A general noncoaxial fabric law and quantitative finite-deformation coupled verification remain pending. Historical coupled finite-load calculations are demonstrations, as recorded in finite-deformation-summary.json.

physical_validation.summary: The parameters are synthetic. No comparison to laboratory or field measurements has been performed.

cases.title: Small-load isotropic Mandel consolidation
cases.description: Coupled displacement and pressure response against the classical analytical solution as the load tends to zero, using parameters that satisfy the compliance restriction. Tolerances under review.

cases.title: Rotated anisotropic consolidation
cases.description: Force-controlled demonstration (top traction plus a kinematic rigid platen) for prescribed mineral orientations on the slender domain [-1,1]x[-0.1,0.1]; compared against the isotropic Mandel reference as a demonstration of the anisotropic material response, not as verification.

cases.title: Partial-boundary drainage
cases.description: Spatially restricted drainage producing two-dimensional flow and deformation on the square domain [-1,1]x[-1,1]. Because the Mandel analytical reference uses the slender domain [-1,1]x[-0.1,0.1], the reference-normalized comparison is not comparable and is omitted; only mass balance, force balance, platen equality, peak pressure, and the maps are reported.

cases.title: Pore-fabric distention probe and rotated-fabric consolidation
cases.description: Reference-state axisymmetric distention law: the Biot tensor, the shape response and the conformal reduction are checked against an independent NumPy implementation of the section equations (worst absolute difference 4.9e-15), and the coupled transient problem is run with the fabric rotated in the plane behind an isotropic, unrotated mineral. The coupled cases are finite-load demonstrations, not quantitative verification of the nonlinear law and not experimental validation.

cases.title: Manufactured-solution and reference-comparison displays
cases.description: The manuscript's finite-element verification claims are displayed from the recorded artifacts: manufactured-solution spatial orders, the fixed-mesh successive-difference temporal orders (measurements that include one value above one; no order above one is asserted), the finite-load pressure floor (about 3.2e-3, a discretization floor), and the constant-reference-tangent Mandel comparison of center pressure and pressure profiles against the independently evaluated series.

reproduction.title: Extract the numerical supplement
reproduction.description: Download the manuscript PDF below. Save its embedded ZIP attachment with an attachment-capable viewer, or use Poppler’s pdfdetach command. The self-contained archive includes numerical sources, parameter matrices, CSV figure data, verification reports, a versioned SHA-256 manifest, and a README with reproduction commands. The repository and downloads also provide the coupled finite-element application, input decks, run analyses, and convergence evidence.

limitations: Stress symmetry alone does not require the dilation-times-rotation specialization at every individual material state; the specialization and volume-only distention energy are additional constitutive assumptions.
The drained and mineral stiffness tensors must obey the spherical rank-one compliance restriction; they are not independent inputs.
The model describes mineral anisotropy; shape-changing distention and pore-shape anisotropy require additional constitutive mechanics.
Rotated-anisotropy and partial-drainage runs are force-controlled demonstrations with a kinematic rigid platen, not verified quantitative predictions.
Parameters are synthetic; agreement with numerical and analytical checks is not experimental validation.

The fabric extension supplies a reference quadratic law and a finite commuting specialization. Full phase-work equivalence at finite deformation requires commuting distention and mineral stress. The scalar comparison is phenomenological and does not supply mineral-volume predictions.

verification_details.title: Independent stress and pressure derivatives
paragraphs: The mineral energy is differentiated in its true frame. Its stress is rotated into the mixture frame and combined with the volume-fraction-weighted fluid stress. Centered differences of the independently evaluated total pressure potential give a separate stress calculation. Differences of solved mineral volume check the pore-volume derivative, and pressure differences of total stress check the instantaneous Biot tensor. Comparisons use complete tensors, including noncoaxial states and repeated stretches.

verification_details.title: Recorded constitutive checks
paragraphs: The spherical-distention suite records 186 named checks, including 65 per-state identities (five states and thirteen identities) and the reference Biot and rank-one compliance relations. The identities cover the true metric, logarithmic strain, rotations, virtual work, volume response, rotated mineral stress, phase balance, and pressure tangent. The largest absolute constitutive-identity error is 2.5 × 10⁻⁹ in nondimensional units. Step refinement of energy, pore-volume, and pressure differences gives second-order convergence before cancellation becomes significant.

The separate tensor suite covers 273 finite states across 13 mineral stiffnesses. The reconstruction suite checks work equivalence, isotropic reductions, reference coefficients, and finite unjacketed compression. These recorded numerical comparisons support implementation verification; they do not establish experimental validity or global stability.

verification_details.title: Admissible volumes and pressure branches
paragraphs: The plotted spherical-distention states satisfy positive phase volumes and the scalar stability condition. At negative pressure, the solver brackets the increasing branch of the mineral equation before its turning point and distinguishes loss of that branch from a violation of positive phase volumes. Independent Lambert-function solutions check admissible negative-pressure states and a large positive-pressure state outside the plotted range. Local scalar stability does not establish stability against every deformation mode. Parameter matrices, loading paths, residuals, software versions, and figure data are recorded with the numerical sources.
